card.title: I Meant to Teach That
card.instruction: Treat any correction, surprise, or improvement as evidence your teaching succeeded. Claim each reversal as the lesson you intended all along.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. You spotted the deliberate error in my recipe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You baked it that way yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A demonstration is more memorable than a warning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Commitment to the lesson. I'm glad you're questioning authority now.

mechanism: A treats corrections to a failed recipe and exposure of their own eating as intended teaching outcomes.
confusable: Unlike defending competence alone, every reversal must be claimed as a lesson deliberately arranged for B.
comparison: S221-a converts eating the error into instructional commitment; S221-b claims being ignored as the highest course outcome.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
